502:  * so that user->allowed_commands[word]&bit will identify that specific
503:  * bit. The function returns C_ERR in case the specified ID overflows
504:  * the bitmap in the user representation. */

506:     if (id >= USER_COMMAND_BITS_COUNT) return C_ERR;
507:     *word = id / sizeof(uint64_t) / 8;
508:     *bit = 1ULL << (id % (sizeof(uint64_t) * 8));

512: /* Check if the specified command bit is set for the specified user.
513:  * The function returns 1 is the bit is set or 0 if it is not.
514:  * Note that this function does not check the ALLCOMMANDS flag of the user
515:  * but just the lowlevel bitmask.

517:  * If the bit overflows the user internal representation, zero is returned
518:  * in order to disallow the execution of the command in such edge case. */

548: /* Remove a rule from the retained command rules. Always match rules
549:  * verbatim, but also remove subcommand rules if we are adding or removing the 
550:  * entire command. */
551: void ACLSelectorRemoveCommandRule(aclSelector *selector, sds new_rule) {
552:     sds rules = selector->command_rules;
553:     uint32_t selector_flags = selector->flags;
554:     unsigned char hdr_flags = rules[-1];
555:     size_t old_len = sdslen(rules);
556:     size_t old_alloc = sdsalloc(rules);
557:     size_t new_len = sdslen(new_rule);
558:     struct redisCommand *cmd = ACLLookupCommand(new_rule);
559: 
560:     /* Command rules are stored as lowercase fullnames. Prefer the command
561:      * object's fullname when it is the same token already being compacted. */
562:     if (cmd && cmd->fullname &&
563:         sdslen(cmd->fullname) == new_len &&
564:         !memcmp(cmd->fullname, new_rule, new_len))
565:     {
566:         new_rule = cmd->fullname;
567:         new_len = sdslen(cmd->fullname);
568:     }
569: 
570:     char *existing_rule = rules;
571: 
572:     /* Loop over the existing rules, trying to find a rule that "matches"
573:      * the new rule. If we find a match, then remove the command from the string by
574:      * copying the later rules over it. */
575:     while(existing_rule[0]) {
576:         /* The first character of the rule is +/-, which we don't need to compare. */
577:         char *copy_position = existing_rule;
578:         existing_rule += 1;
579: 
580:         /* Assume a trailing space after a command is part of the command, like '+get ', so trim it
581:          * as well if the command is removed. */
582:         char *rule_end = strchr(existing_rule, ' ');
583:         if (!rule_end) {
584:             /* This is the last rule, so it it to the end of the string. */
585:             rule_end = existing_rule + strlen(existing_rule);
586: 
587:             /* This approach can leave a trailing space if the last rule is removed,
588:              * but only if it's not the first rule, so handle that case. */
589:             if (copy_position != selector->command_rules) copy_position -= 1;
590:         }
591:         char *copy_end = rule_end;
592:         if (*copy_end == ' ') copy_end++;
593: 
594:         /* Exact match or the rule we are comparing is a subcommand denoted by '|' */
595:         size_t existing_len = rule_end - existing_rule;
596:         if (!memcmp(existing_rule, new_rule, min(existing_len, new_len))) {
597:             if ((existing_len == new_len) || (existing_len > new_len && (existing_rule[new_len]) == '|')) {
598:                 /* Copy the remaining rules starting at the next rule to replace the rule to be
599:                  * deleted, including the terminating NULL character. */
600:                 memmove(copy_position, copy_end, strlen(copy_end) + 1);
601:             }
602:         }
603:         existing_rule = copy_end;
604:     }

606:     /* After compacting the rule buffer in place, write the remaining
607:      * C-string length back into the SDS header. ALLCOMMANDS selectors
608:      * still keep an ordered override list, so an already-empty string
609:      * only needs a header sync when the logical length may have changed. */
610:     size_t real_len = strlen(rules);
611:     serverAssert(real_len <= old_len);
612:     serverAssert(real_len <= old_alloc);
613:     if (!(selector_flags & SELECTOR_FLAG_ALLCOMMANDS) || real_len != 0 || old_len != 0) {
614:         switch(hdr_flags & SDS_TYPE_MASK) {
615:             case SDS_TYPE_5: {

618:                 break;
619:             }
620:             case SDS_TYPE_8:
621:                 SDS_HDR(8,rules)->len = real_len;
622:                 break;
623:             case SDS_TYPE_16:
624:                 SDS_HDR(16,rules)->len = real_len;
625:                 break;
626:             case SDS_TYPE_32:
627:                 SDS_HDR(32,rules)->len = real_len;
628:                 break;
629:             case SDS_TYPE_64:
630:                 SDS_HDR(64,rules)->len = real_len;

769:  * rules related to command execution, in the same format you could set them
770:  * back using ACL SETUSER. The function will return just the set of rules needed
771:  * to recreate the user commands bitmap, without including other user flags such
772:  * as on/off, passwords and so forth. The returned string always starts with
773:  * the +@all or -@all rule, depending on the user bitmap, and is followed, if
774:  * needed, by the other rules needed to narrow or extend what the user can do. */
775: sds ACLDescribeSelectorCommandRules(aclSelector *selector) {
776:     sds rules = sdsempty();
777: 
778:     /* We use this fake selector as a "sanity" check to make sure the rules
779:      * we generate have the same bitmap as those on the current selector. */
780:     aclSelector *fake_selector = ACLCreateSelector(0);
781: 
782:     /* Here we want to understand if we should start with +@all or -@all.
783:      * Note that when starting with +@all and subtracting, the user
784:      * will be able to execute future commands, while -@all and adding will just
785:      * allow the user the run the selected commands and/or categories.
786:      * How do we test for that? We use the trick of a reserved command ID bit
787:      * that is set only by +@all (and its alias "allcommands"). */

789:         rules = sdscat(rules,"+@all ");
790:         ACLSetSelector(fake_selector,"+@all",-1);

792:         rules = sdscat(rules,"-@all ");

797:     int argc = 0;
798:     sds *argv = sdssplitargs(selector->command_rules, &argc);
799:     serverAssert(argv != NULL);

801:     for(int i = 0; i < argc; i++) {
802:         int res = ACLSetSelector(fake_selector, argv[i], -1);
803:         serverAssert(res == C_OK);
804:     }
805:     if (sdslen(selector->command_rules)) {
806:         rules = sdscatfmt(rules, "%S ", selector->command_rules);

814:      * predicted bitmap is exactly the same as the user bitmap, and abort
